subject.title: fix(codex): restore native PreToolUse relay delivery

question: Should OpenClaw merge this positive-delivery path once Code Mode normalization is fixed, given it depends on a Codex runtime that emits Code Mode PreToolUse and routes policy-active turns through unified exec/fresh thread binding?
rationale: The remaining choice is not only mechanical: it affects tool-execution security boundaries, Codex runtime assumptions, and session compatibility for existing policy-active users.

options.title: Fix normalization, then accept positive delivery
options.body: Add the missing `code_mode_exec` to `exec` mapping and proceed if maintainers accept the patched Codex runtime and session tradeoff.

options.title: Wait for packaged Codex proof
options.body: Keep the PR draft until the OpenClaw-supported Codex package/runtime emits the required Code Mode PreToolUse payload without local patch assumptions.

options.title: Prefer fail-closed replacement
options.body: Pause or close this path if maintainers prefer the fail-closed canary approach in #90805 or the broader mitigation in #90633.

recommendation.title: Fix normalization, then accept positive delivery
recommendation.body: Add the missing `code_mode_exec` to `exec` mapping and proceed if maintainers accept the patched Codex runtime and session tradeoff.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has adjacent merged native-hook relay fallback history and is the best available owner signal for the runtime/security tradeoff if a maintainer choice is needed.
